subject.title: Feature: Per-call cost tracking & auth profile attribution

question: Should OpenClaw make resolved auth-profile attribution part of the canonical completed-model-call accounting contract, and which surfaces may expose it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix chooses privacy, storage, gateway/API, diagnostics, plugin, UI, and transcript exposure boundaries for credential-adjacent billing metadata.

options.title: Design canonical attribution contract
options.body: Record resolved authProfileId and cost at the normalized completed-call seam, expose only redacted/additive readers, and make this the source for status, usage, diagnostics, UI, and plugin views.

options.title: Limit exposure to plugin or diagnostics first
options.body: Keep native transcript/status/usage unchanged for now and expose safe model usage metadata only through an explicit maintainer-approved observer capability.

options.title: Defer native attribution
options.body: Keep current provider/model cost summaries and external workarounds such as burn0 until maintainers are ready to own credential-adjacent attribution metadata.

recommendation.title: Design canonical attribution contract
recommendation.body: Record resolved authProfileId and cost at the normalized completed-call seam, expose only redacted/additive readers, and make this the source for status, usage, diagnostics, UI, and plugin views.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on the existing usage-cost summaries and prior review of this exact attribution gap.
